systems.title: Fleet deployment and cargo custody
systems.model: PlayerShip_t retains a pilot and deployed flag. Escort_t distinguishes owned fleet ships from bay craft. PilotCommodity records commodity, quantity and mission cargo ID. Fleet capacity and fleet_used are separate player fields.
systems.rules: pfleet_update sums current hull points plus points of deployed owned ships. Cargo free/used includes fleet escorts only when fleet_capacity > 0. Redistribution merges ordinary identical goods, keeps mission cargo separate, sorts mission cargo first then descending base commodity price. Mission cargo is added to the flagship; ordinary cargo goes through fleet distribution. While landed, overflow may be placed on the flagship. Undeploy checks capacity of the remaining fleet and asks before a shortage-producing shrink. A debug warning is not a conservation guarantee.
systems.connections: Owned ships are deployed as escort AI and get automatic weapon sets; cargo transfers affect mission eligibility and travel mass. Ordinary goods and objective payloads have different placement policy.
systems.authoring: Hull XML supplies points and cargo stats. Native pfleet_toggleDeploy, pfleet_deploy and pfleet_cargoRedistributeInternal implement transitions; script orders are a separate layer.
systems.persistence: player_saveShip writes model, name, deployed, fuel, outfits, cargo, acquisition metadata and shipvars. player_saveEscorts persists bay model or fleet name only when e.persist. Load resolves owned fleet ships and checks spaceworthiness; live escort task stacks are not serialized by these records.
systems.unread: Full capacity UI admission, cargo discard quantities, deployed death settlement and every fleet API remain unread. Source-traced allocation is not a tested stock invariant.

systems.title: Capture is a pending recovery process
systems.model: board.lua calculates a quote; naev.cache().capture_pilot passes pilot, cost, costnaked and outfitsnaked into the event. Event mem stores ship, name, system, original faction/name, filtered outfits, intrinsics and quotes. A cloned pilot invalidates old references.
systems.rules: is_capturable refuses noplayer hulls, carried fighters and actors neither natural nor explicitly capturable. Quote factor is (10 + target crew)/(12 + player crew)/loot_mod. Start with worth; subtract nosteal nonlocked outfit prices from full cost and all nonlocked prices from stripped cost, then multiply; stripped quote is min(full, stripped*factor). Capture removes nosteal outfits, disables and tethers the clone. Added player mass is half captured mass. In drag(dt), outside radius*1.2+20, acceleration is normalized relative position times (target distance - actual distance)*player mass/captured mass. A refuel service without noshipcapture offers full repair, stripped repair, or damaged retention. Insufficient money still retains a damaged hull.
systems.connections: This separates encounter control, travel burden, final ownership and usable equipment. Death/abandon clears drag; landing creates an owned ship with captured shipvar and provenance.
systems.authoring: Lua event plus board UI and hull/outfit tags. evt.save(true) requests event persistence. No generic human recruitment or consent model follows from vehicle capture.
systems.persistence: Pending terms live in saved event mem, while event enter reconstructs a pilot from retained definitions. At settlement owned-ship serializer carries the result. Active pilot/update hooks are transient and must be reconstructed by lifecycle code. Exact mid-tow restore and callback interruption remain untested.
systems.unread: No crash-atomic capture/payment claim. loot_mod upstream derivation and all capture blockers outside is_capturable remain partial.

systems.title: Deferred repair preserves an impaired asset
systems.model: Unrepaired captured ships receive the Heavily Damaged intrinsic and per-ship repair_cost. Ship Repairs is a load-triggered event that searches the current ship and player.ships for this outfit.
systems.rules: The repair NPC appears only at a shipyard and only with damaged ships. A dynamic menu lists actual repairable ships and reads each saved quote. Credits < cost refuses without debit. Otherwise pay(-cost), remove the intrinsic from the chosen ship, temporarily swapping if necessary, then return to the original ship. The menu repeats until no ships remain, then removes the NPC. This is a paid removal of a damage marker, not timed component fabrication.
systems.connections: Capture can end usefully without funds; later wealth and a fitting service restore use. The stripped capture path does not restore lost noncritical outfits through this repair.
systems.authoring: Event Lua is a service wrapper around actual owned ships. One intrinsic identifies impairment and one shipvar stores the accepted future price.
systems.persistence: Intrinsic and quote are covered by player_saveShip outfit and shipvar domains. The NPC is reconstructed on landing/load; persistent NPC identity or arbitrary VN cursor is not required by this service.
systems.unread: Repair does not clear repair_cost in this script; absence of the marker removes it from eligible ships. Missing or corrupt quote behavior and interrupted payment are unverified.

systems.title: Convoy contracts, survival and orders
systems.model: escort.init retains mem._escort with original/current ship lists, faction, parameters, convoy handles and hook IDs. setDest adds destination system/place, route, current index, nextsys and named success/failure callback.
systems.rules: One-second heartbeat commands land or jump when within 2000 units of the target. Death removes corresponding convoy and ship-list entries; nofailifdead changes the all-dead failure policy. Jump/land handlers account for actual departures; entering the wrong next system invokes failure. Route index advances on jumpin. Player order menu sends e_hold, e_return or e_clear and uses drone-specific acknowledgement. These are orders, not relationships.
systems.connections: Companion participation has a place, route, surviving members and explicit completion. Mission author can pay according to survivors. Owned fleets, bay fighters and temporary mission escorts are distinct custody paths.
systems.authoring: Lua helper takes hull lists or existing pilots and named callback functions; followorders, nofollowplayer and per-pilot callbacks customize it. Existing-pilot outfit snapshot is a module-local escort_outfits, explicitly commented session-only.
systems.persistence: Mission mem retains route and survivors, but the snapshot of original outfits is not saved globally. spawn recreates live actors and hooks; transient pilot/timer handles are not a durable actor identity. This closes basic escort structure, not exact companion persistence.
systems.unread: All callers, autonomous combat plans, relationship memory, hireling wages and guaranteed exact reload equipment remain open. No generic hireling economy was located in selected helpers.

systems.title: NPC equipment as constrained choice
systems.model: Outfit cache records specific stats, broad/type categories, price, limit, mass and CPU. Candidate slot/outfit pairs become binary linear-program columns; hull stats, chosen cores and parameter weights form the context.
systems.rules: Objective maximizes weighted goodness. Weapon component begins 0.5*(DPS*damageWeight + disable*disableWeight), then accounts for tracking, range, absorption, lock-on and family preferences. Rows constrain CPU, energy, mass, negative energy-regeneration modifiers, optional budget, limits and one outfit per slot. energygoal=max((1-min_energy_regen)*baseRegen,min_energy_regen_abs); massgoal=max(max_mass*engine_limit-baseMass,engine_limit*min_mass_margin). It solves, equips and checks actual post-equip regeneration. Up to five attempts restore base equipment and adjust emod by 1.5 on regeneration failure; infeasible solves may double mass tolerance and relax/remove nebula regeneration requirements. This is approximate optimization with fallback, not hard proof all spawned ships satisfy every ideal constraint.
systems.connections: Miner template prefers mining lances, sets disable weight zero, and gives drill preference a 20% roll. Faction wrappers choose pools and cores. Some special ships bypass the solver entirely.
systems.authoring: Lua templates, parameter tables and candidate pools, backed by linopt. Author can tune roles without hand-authoring every loadout. Tiny hardcoded overrides qualify the generic objective.
systems.persistence: Solver variables/cache are derived generation state, not a saved plan. Owned results serialize as actual equipped outfits; generic spawned pilots need not persist. No claim a random future outfit choice repeats after reload.
systems.unread: All faction templates, exact solver backend behavior and fallback spaceworthiness remain unread/unexecuted.

systems.title: Bioship skill graph and respecialization
systems.model: Skill records carry tier, requires, replaces, outfit, slot and display data. _getskills resolves requirement/reverse links and intrinsic stages. Five default families are bite, health, attack, misc and plasma; movement, stealth and carrier families depend on size/tags.
systems.rules: Max skill tier is 3, 4 if size>2, 5 if size>4. Movement is added for size<=3; stealth for size<=4 or its tag; carrier by tag. Threshold for stage s is sum over i=1..s-1 of floor(300*1.2^(i-1)). Free points = stage - enabled nonzero-tier skills. Player activation requires landing, a free point and enabled prerequisites. skill_enable installs slot or intrinsic equipment and stores bio_<key>. Reset charges floor(0.2*current XP), recalculates stage, removes skill effects and rebuilds the window. It can lower stage.
systems.connections: Actual hull form constrains available faculties; earned state and installed organs/equipment are separate. ship_intrinsics falls back to parent hull definition through inherits. That is definition inheritance, not biological descent.
systems.authoring: bioship.skills and bioship.intrinsics are Lua definitions; helpers install/remove actual outfits and resolve replacement links. NPC simulate chooses random eligible skills and heals the generated pilot.
systems.persistence: XP, stage and bio_ flags are shipvars; manager reconstruction was covered earlier. Installed outfit effects are saved too. The graph is rebuilt from current definitions, so content changes require the manager compatibility repairs.
systems.unread: All individual skill effects and replacement dependency cases remain partial. No breeding, genome, child or family-lineage implementation is established by these files.

systems.title: Mining method, yield and optional timing interaction
systems.model: AsteroidType holds armour range, absorb, material reward rows with quantity/rarity and scanned message. Group XML weights asteroid types; system fields instantiate anchors. The optional mining interaction has targets with angular position, size, sway, reward and depth, and a callback supplied by its caller.
systems.rules: Iron-Nickel authored armour is 80..120 with absorb 30; reward rows are Iron 25, Nickel 25 and Silicate 5. typeA-standard weights are 6/3/1. Hit absorption factor is 0.99^max(0,absorb-penetration). Explosion filters rewards by max_rarity, chooses ONE eligible material uniformly, then rolls nb in [0,round(quantity*mining_bonus)]. Each gatherable has random quantity 1..5, so nb is not final tonnage. Explosion alerts nearby pilots and respawns the asteroid elsewhere with a 0.5 transition timer. This is renewable field generation, not conserved finite geology. Optional timing minigame defaults to speed pi radians/sec and three shots. Hit requires matching depth and abs(pointer-target angle)<target size; bonus=sum(hit reward)/target count. Completion calls reward_func once per loaded interaction.
systems.connections: Extraction result depends on tool rarity/bonus and collection capacity. Exploration/scan tells the player about deposits. Optional active interaction is separate from ordinary weapon extraction and from an idle policy.
systems.authoring: XML types/groups and native asteroid_hit/explode; Lua mining wrapper can run standalone or as custom VN state. Wrapper comment calls it Sokoban, but core implements a rotating pointer.
systems.persistence: Cargo results serialize through ships. Asteroid live position, armour, scan state and timing-minigame locals are not included in the inspected player serializer. No exact deposit depletion or pending-minigame save contract established.
systems.unread: Gatherable lifetime/pickup rules and drill callback conversion of bonus to actual stock remain unread. No claim zero-yield roll is protected by pity.

systems.title: POI leads, scanner trails and fixed reward identity
systems.model: poi.generate returns sys, risk and optional reward module. Startup transfers temporary _poi_* variables into mission mem.sys/risk/reward. Reward records have type, value, weight, optional ship/name and module name. mem.poi holds target, callback name, markers and scanner hook.
systems.rules: Eligible systems are softly claimable, volatility<=25, with no place both landable and inhabited; sample within 1..5 jumps. risk=min(Poisson(1.5),5,completed POIs). However mission create stores rewardrisk, THEN forces mem.risk=2 and locked=true. Credit reward is (100000+100000*U)*(rewardrisk*0.5+1); credits weight .5, or .05 with lucky state, other rows default 1. Selected reward is retained at create. On entry initial trail point is radius*.6 at a random angle; 13..17 segments have lengths 600+300*U, plus final 600+400*U. Scan requires <=3000 units; trail points and goal require <1000 and sequential reveal, checked each second. Locked boarding invokes stringguess; failure closes without reward. Enter event has 5% metadata chance and 5..15 second local delay.
systems.connections: Leads arrive through NPCs or naturally spawned boarded pilots. Patron route has 5% chance, prior completion, independent presence, generic unrestricted port and fewer than three active POIs. The board route lacks that same three-active check in this file. Rewards can be inventory data, money, outfits or authored module functions. Data acquired total and current owned data differ.
systems.authoring: common.poi hosts trail/boarding logic; reward directory functions can refuse eligibility or return weighted records. Stable chosen reward does not mean a stable geometric trail.
systems.persistence: Mission mem preserves reward identity and terms; _poi_* variables are consumed on startup. Goal is assigned to mem but trail positions, started flag and visual path are module locals regenerated on enter. Inventory and poi_data_gained/known are separate retained domains. No arbitrary mid-trail or puzzle cursor restoration guarantee.
systems.unread: All reward modules, stringguess algorithms, fresh-load trail behavior and interruption atomicity remain open. Source override contradicts reading generated risk as actual encounter difficulty.

systems.title: Discovery records are more than map knowledge
systems.model: Discovery table entries specify type (enter, distance, discover), variable name, title/subtitle, optional position/radius, asset or callback. Separate tables key on system, faction or custom predicate.
systems.rules: handle_event ignores already recorded variables. Distance entries poll every .5 seconds and fire at distance<authored dist, commonly 5000. discover_trigger refuses during cinematics, appends a travel log, resets autonav for 3, executes optional callback, pushes a variable and shows a title/audio cue. Some callbacks mark factions known and rename visible Unknown pilots. create uses hasevent = hasevent or handle_event(...); Lua short-circuit means after a truthy result later eligible handlers are not evaluated in that call. Do not assume every simultaneous discovery queues.
systems.connections: Purchased maps, sensor detection, physical approach, faction recognition and flavour acknowledgement can differ. This extends the prior proximity example with a mechanical information callback and selection-order caveat.
systems.authoring: Lua tables plus named predicates/callbacks. A custom atmosphere tag can nominate a discovery without a new native trigger.
systems.persistence: var and shiplog persist through their existing save domains; temporary .5-second timers and on-screen overlays do not. Reentry can reconstruct pending checks, subject to recorded flag and branch order.
systems.unread: Runtime cinematics retry and competing discoveries not reproduced. This source uses one-time flavour flags; YAIRPG should not copy a lifetime event restriction onto recurring useful content.

systems.title: Knowledge-gated reference pages
systems.model: Naevpedia .md files have YAML metadata title, priority and cond; parser also organizes category, entry and parent. Page text supports Lua statements, expressions and widget functions. Event registers Archives info button and A shortcut.
systems.rules: Readme STATED pipeline: extract YAML, translate lines except pure Lua, expand Lua, parse CommonMark. Source SHOWN test_cond runs compiled condition under pcall; an error warns and hides the entry. Navigation filters category and conditions, orders parent/child, then priority (default 5, lower first), then translated title or filename. Dynamic body content reads current known state. Inline expressions execute in page environment, so rendering is executable content, not a declarative safety boundary.
systems.connections: Reference pages can reveal only known ship/faction information and use actual descriptions. This helps avoid a separate static encyclopaedia that leaks every definition or drifts from mechanics.
systems.authoring: Writers add .md, YAML gates and optional Lua-generated text/widgets. Readme explicitly says .markdown files are excluded. Localization happens before Lua/Markdown rendering.
systems.persistence: Underlying known flags and actor state persist; pages and cached metadata are derived. No new learned skill is awarded by opening a page in the inspected registration path. Reading-history/notebook progress is not established.
systems.unread: All page gates, search/accessibility and widget side effects remain partial; no rendered desktop evidence.

systems.title: Technology catalogues are local supply, not research
systems.model: tech_item_t distinguishes outfit, ship, commodity, group and group-pointer; holds avail string/compiled chunk, avail_search and price_mod. tech_group contains name, source filename and item array.
systems.rules: Two-pass loader creates named groups before resolving members. Unspecified item type is resolved through tech lookup; explicit type chooses group/outfit/ship/commodity. Defaults: avail_search=0, price_mod=1. In actual availability mode (search=0), a false condition skips an item; search mode skips conditional entries without avail_search, rather than enforcing the same live predicate. search<0 bypasses these checks. Recursive expansion de-duplicates entries; price reader can replace a duplicate modifier when the later encountered modifier differs from 1. No per-player research points or prerequisite-learning tree is defined by tech.c.
systems.connections: Place services decide which store exists; catalogue decides its goods; reputation/license/payability still have their own readers. World diffs can change tech access, extending the earlier colony stage trace.
systems.authoring: XML tech groups compose reusable lists and conditional items. Read tech_addGroupItemPrice for recursion and mode semantics, not just directory name.
systems.persistence: Catalogues reload from content; selected world diffs are saved. Purchased goods serialize as inventory/equipment. Runtime catalogue API mutation is not automatically a persistent diff; its author must use a retained path.
systems.unread: All nested conditional combinations, cyclic-group handling and every shop purchase validator remain unread.

systems.title: Sensing, scanning and stealth are different states
systems.model: Pilot stores ew_detection, ew_signature, ew_stealth, scan timer and stealth timer; ShipStats supplies detection/tracking/hide multipliers. Local asteroid/jump interference and hull mass enter derived radii.
systems.rules: Normal pilot range returns 1 for identified contact, -1 for fuzzy detection, 0 for none: d²<(observer detect*track*target signature)², else d²<(observer detect*target detection)². Nonallied stealthed contacts return 0 here, with explicit visibility/parent exceptions earlier. Scan time helper is mass^(1/3)*1.25/(ew_hide*ew_signature)*ew_scanned_time; ScanStart passes the scanning pilot, so do not silently reinterpret it as target mass. Timer decrements only within identification range and fires scan/scanned hooks below zero. Stealth with no nearby breakers recovers by dt*5000/stealthRadius capped at 1; with breakers drains dt*(stealthRadius/10000+nearbyMod)*timerStat, and reveals below zero. Entry refuses nearby breakers and turns off weapons/outfits. Missile-lock admission check is commented out.
systems.connections: Perception controls reliable information and patrol callbacks. Scan effects, cargo illegality and autonav interruption connect observations to consequences. A UI message for lock-on failure does not prove the commented guard executes.
systems.authoring: Native EW readers with hull/outfit stats; Lua callbacks can react to scan events. Nearby-breaker eligibility is its own helper, not just all ships in radius.
systems.persistence: Outfits and permanent knowledge can persist; transient scan/stealth timers and flags are absent from the inspected player_saveShip body. Do not claim exact in-flight EW restoration.
systems.unread: Every nearby-breaker exception, weapon lock-on/accuracy model and post-scan knowledge memory remain partial.

systems.title: Timed effects and typed damage
systems.model: EffectData contains duration, overwrite group, priority, stats, buff/debuff flags and Lua callbacks. Effect instance adds timer, elapsed, strength, parent and applicator. Damage type definitions are TOML at this pin; Rust exposes C ABI calculation.
systems.rules: effect_add uses passed duration only if >0, otherwise definition duration. It matches overwrite group only where new priority<=existing priority. For the SAME definition, weaker strength is ignored; equal strength with a longer existing timer is ignored; accepted repeat resets timer and invokes extend callback. Different definitions in a matching group invoke old removal then replacement, without comparing incomparable strength. No overwrite group allows separate instances. effect_update subtracts dt; effect_compute scales stat merges by strength. dtype_calcDamage returns typeMultiplier*damage*absorb*max(0,1-resistanceStat) when configured, otherwise resistance factor 1. Kinetic TOML shield=.8, armour=1.15. This helper does not by itself specify shield overflow or disable recovery.
systems.connections: Equipment, attacks and temporary status modifiers share actual stat readers. Parent/applicator retain causal actor references while alive; not proof of long-term injury or social blame.
systems.authoring: XML effects with optional Lua handlers; TOML damage types and optional resistance stat. Plasma Burn sample duration is 5, debuff, damage stat .2. Do not translate that stat into total DPS without tracing its consumer.
systems.persistence: Inspected player ship serialization saves installed outfits and shipvars, not an effect list or effect timers. Treat effects as transient for this inspected save route; every alternate snapshot path remains outside scope.
systems.unread: All effects, damage application overflow, disable/stress, heat, difficulty presets and lingering injury remain partial.

systems.title: Gates and wormholes have distinct travel contracts
systems.model: Hypergate setup has destination function, cost_flat (10000), cost_mass (50), cost_mod (1) and appearance. Default destinations enumerate active hypergate-tagged places in other systems. Wormhole setup accepts fixed target or function and local parameters.
systems.rules: Hypergate quote = floor(flat*modifier+.5) + totalMass*floor(perMass*modifier+.5), with mass of player and followers. A modifier table searches from floor(local standing) toward zero for first authored entry. Unknown destinations get stable-looking signature labels and can still be chosen after warning. Confirmation requires credits>cost, so exact equality fails in this pin. Pay precedes event. Hypergate event teleports immediately then runs a 4-real-second visual; its comment warns enter hooks can interact. Wormhole uses per-ship wormhole marker to avoid double landing, a cached target, two 2-real-second visual halves and at crossing advances local game time by time.new(0,0,1000+2000*U), then teleports and clears the marker.
systems.connections: Knowledge, faction terms, fleet size, destination and elapsed game time affect travel independently. Four visual seconds are not four game seconds or a universal crossing rate.
systems.authoring: Shared Lua place modules expose hooks; each authored gate/wormhole wrapper supplies target/terms. Changed active tags can come from world diffs.
systems.persistence: Hypergate target uses var, wormhole target uses naev.cache; update timers, local target and shaders are transient and neither event requests evt.save here. Completed location, credits and shipvars use normal owners. Pending crossing recovery is not established, especially a stranded wormhole marker.
systems.unread: Ordinary jump/fuel admission, all wrappers, transport fleets, hypergate construction and interrupted crossing remain unread.

systems.title: Price motion and remembered market samples
systems.model: CommodityPrice has base price, system/place variations and periods plus sample sum, sum2, count and update time. Commodity supports constant price or reference price multiplied by a modifier.
systems.rules: economy_getPriceAtTime first resolves reference/constant branches. For ordinary goods, t=converted game seconds/NT_PERIOD_SECONDS; price=max(1,round(base+sysVariation*sin(2*pi*t/sysPeriod)+spobVariation*sin(2*pi*t/spobPeriod))). Missing local listing falls back to average price. Initial regional shaping multiplies base by 1+radius/200000, 1+nebulaVolatility/600 and 1+interference/10000, then smooths place/system/neighbor prices. This formula supplies periodic opportunity, not measured shortage. economy_getAverageSpobPrice uses stored samples and current catalogue price modifiers; mean and variance summarize observations.
systems.connections: Known market history and current world truth differ. Cargo capacity, route cost and deadlines determine useful arbitrage. No conserved merchant warehouse or autonomous factory chain is established by this engine.
systems.authoring: Commodity XML, place metadata, system topology and catalogue modifiers configure price fields; native economy_init performs smoothing. News may describe computed prices, not independent causes.
systems.persistence: economy_sysSave writes lastPurchase prices and only observed place/commodity sample sum,sum2,cnt,time. Formula fields are derived from content and current game time. Owned stock belongs to ship cargo, not this sample history.
systems.unread: Every initialization coefficient and trading UI accounting, recursive reference cycles, actual purchase quantity curves and restock semantics remain partial.
